notes:
I couldn't do this research. My tools hit their usage limit before any pages loaded, so I didn't read a single source on Isaiah 32. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from memory, so I haven't written any notes. Notes from memory would have no real URLs behind them and could put words in a commentator's mouth.

On the next try I'd load one page at a time instead of all at once, starting with the main verse-by-verse sources:

- **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word (Guzik), Biblehub's Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Gill and Barnes pages for Isaiah 32, StudyLight (Matthew Henry), and Precept Austin.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu) and Spurgeon sermons on verses 2, 15 and 17. Desiring God, Grace to You and Ligonier on verse 1 (does the king mean Hezekiah or the Messiah?) and verse 15 (the Spirit poured out, Pentecost, and the end times). Reformed, Lutheran, Pentecostal and premillennial readers may differ on these. I'd also check Pneuma Review, Sam Storms and the AG site for Pentecostal readings of verse 15.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes for wording issues in verses 4–8, 14 and 19, and Bible Odyssey for dating and authorship. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, I'd check New Advent (Church Fathers) and Catholic.com, especially for messianic or Marian uses of verse 2 and the Spirit in verse 15.

I'd only write a point where a page I've read supports it, with its URL. If a tradition or view doesn't come up for a verse, I'll leave it out. If you'd like, I can start with verses 1–8 to keep each step small.
